generation_review.prompt:
You are designing an original Small Seal Gothic monoline font glyph using historical evidence. The attached image is a reference sheet for ONE Unicode character with FOUR historical specimen views labelled THX, CCZ, QJZ, DYC. Some views may be marked UNAVAILABLE. Create exactly ONE new standalone glyph for this character. Study ALL AVAILABLE specimens equally and understand their actual stroke courses. Preserve the character's attested identity, all essential branches, counters, crossings, and disconnected stroke separations. Do not trace or mimic any individual brush silhouette; do not favor THX. If source variants differ structurally choose one coherent attested structure informed by their shared identity; never combine incompatible variants or replace an ancient glyph with a modern Chinese form. Draw genuine flowing stroke paths, smoothly rounded curves and joins, circular rounded terminals, black and constant-width throughout, about 4 percent of the full square canvas width. No brush texture, no taper, no calligraphic contrast, no serif flares, no filled decorations. The glyph should be well balanced and centered in the central 70 percent of the square transparent canvas with generous margins. Output ONLY ONE black glyph on transparency: no specimen copies, no four-panel layout, no labels, no letters or numbers, no title, no grid, no background, no border. Smooth vector-like clean monoline strokes.
Specific U+3D018: LEFT has short detached upper bar above longer lower bar with three descending legs (center attached, outer pair detached). RIGHT has three distinct levels. Top right: a small open-top U shape with a taller left upright and a short right upright curving at the base. The left upright continues slightly below the U base, turns smoothly right and forms a second longer horizontal baseline; the top motif stays OPEN above, not a closed box. Middle right: a separate tall rounded rectangular eye with TWO internal horizontal rungs, giving exactly THREE stacked white counters. Outside the eye at left is a separate long bracket-like stroke: it starts level with eye top, descends down its left side, then rounds right under the eye into a long horizontal support. Bottom right: TWO short descending legs attached underneath that support, curving apart to left and right as coherently attested by THX and CCZ; do not blend the no-leg QJZ or one-leg DYC variant into this. Use all four specimens to preserve the shared top and eye identity. Keep eye separate from surrounding left-under bracket; keep top motif separate from eye. All strokes uniform4%canvas with rounded caps and smooth curves.
generation_review.evidence_policy: All available THX, CCZ, QJZ, DYC views studied equally. UNAVAILABLE is not evidence. No incompatible hybrid.
generation_review.review_notes: Compared all four views. Shared open upper U/extended left-stem baseline, separate 3-counter eye and separate left-under bracket retained. Two-foot lower structure coherently chosen from THX/CCZ rather than blending QJZ no-foot and DYC single-foot variants.

notes: All four enlarged specimens THX, CCZ, QJZ and DYC show the lower free horizontal of the upper-right motif extending rightward beyond the upper U hook. The native drawing instead ends this lower bar before the hook right edge.
The native PNG remains unchanged and mismatched; acceptance applies only to corrected vector geometry. The existing coherent THX/CCZ two-foot lower variant is preserved.
